llm.summary: The skill's code and runtime instructions match its declared purpose (deregistering Consul services via HTTP), with only minor usability/clarity issues rather than security mismatches.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Consul deregister) align with the provided script and instructions. The script implements HTTP PUT requests to /v1/agent/service/deregister and supports service-id, agents list/file, parsing curl, ACL token, dry-run, and parallelism — all consistent with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run the included Python script and describes expected modes. Two minor concerns: (1) SKILL.md uses a hard-coded absolute path (/Users/shiheng/.qclaw/...) which is user-specific and may be incorrect on other hosts; (2) the 'Common Workflows' text (e.g., 'AI finds the old version's service ID from config/docs') is vague and could be interpreted as giving the agent broad discretion to search user files for IDs. The script itself does not perform file-system discovery beyond reading an agents file when explicitly passed.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; this is an instruction-only skill with one included Python script. Nothing is downloaded or installed at runtime by the skill manifest. Risk is limited to the script being executed locally.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or secrets in the manifest. The script accepts an optional --token argument for Consul ACL tokens (appropriate and proportional). It does not read other env vars or system credentials.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no install-time persistence or modifications to other skills. Agent autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but not combined with other red flags.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: send HTTP PUT requests to Consul agents to deregister service IDs. Before using it: 1) Prefer --dry-run first to verify the resolved URLs and targets. 2) Double-check the agent list you pass (or the agents.txt file) — the script will send requests to any host you provide. 3) If you need to pass an ACL token, supply it explicitly via --token; the skill does not read stored credentials. 4) SKILL.md references an absolute author-specific path (/Users/shiheng/.qclaw/...), so adjust the command to the actual script location on your system. 5) The text about the AI finding service IDs in config/docs is vague — do not allow the agent to autonomously search your files unless you intend it to. 6) If you will grant autonomous invocation to this skill, be aware it can initiate network requests to arbitrary hosts you supply; restrict usage or review commands before execution.
